A package-level declaration initializer — a const, or a var whose composite literal is built at init — is evaluated before any instrumented statement runs, so go-cover emits no coverage block for its line at all: not a block with count 0, no block. Gremlins only builds and runs mutants on lines the profile shows as covered, so such a line's mutant is never compiled, never run, and can never be killed by any test a caller could write. Proven by TestConstInitializerHasNoCoverageBlock in internal/mutation/ceiling_test.go (the fixture's const line sits in no block while its statement lines do) and by TestNoCoverageBlockIsNotACoverageGap in internal/survivor/evidence_test.go, which pins the distinction from an ordinary coverage gap — a gap is a block that never ran, and a test can close it. Distinct from the attribution ceiling: there the line runs and the tool disagrees; here the line is structurally uninstrumentable.
